# UI, Accessibility, And Settings

- Edit source `shell.html`, `pre.js`, and relevant graphics/interop code, not generated outputs (`ucblogo.html`, `sw.js`). Rebuild with `emmake make` (or `npm run build:web` for a clean build) before browser tests; if a browser still shows old markup, use the [stale-artifacts checklist](../../ucb-logo-web-testing/references/stale-artifacts.md). Preserve existing UI/CSS conventions.
- Prefer native HTML labels and semantics. Associate every form label with its control, use `fieldset`/`legend` for related radio choices, and add ARIA only when native semantics do not provide the needed name or state. Give dialogs `aria-labelledby` headings and meaningful live/status regions.
- For dialog layouts with persistent title bars, keep the heading as a direct dialog child and put independently scrollable content in a separate body wrapper. Use modal `showModal()` where modal behavior is intended; verify focus entry/restoration and that scrolling the body does not move the title bar.
- Emscripten or application code may replace DOM nodes after startup. When adding roles, accessible names, or focusability to a node such as terminal output, inspect all replacement/creation paths and apply the same semantics there; template markup alone may not survive.
- Use `click` for native button activation so touch, keyboard, and assistive-technology activation share one path. For insertion controls, preserve the target text field's selection semantics, restore focus, and place the caret after the inserted text. Keep touch-target dimensions appropriate to the existing mobile layout.
- Test accessibility semantics in a real browser: inspect computed accessible names/roles, modal focus behavior, and computed layout/scroll ownership, not only source strings. A syntax check of inline scripts can catch template-literal quoting mistakes that otherwise appear as unrelated missing controls and failed UI tests.
- Validate affected terminal, editor, dialogs, settings, focus/history, keyboard/touch/mobile input, resize/themes, accessibility, and error display. Check SVG/DOM graphics and assets in a real browser.
- For terminal BEL (`\x07`) handling in Web Edition output, pair audible tone with a visual cue in `shell.html` `Module.print(...args)`: use a high-contrast `role="status"` / `aria-live="polite"` indicator, debounce repeated bells by extending one visibility timer, and avoid rapid flashes (prefer a gentle fade and honor `prefers-reduced-motion`).
- Distinguish ordinary text from intentional HTML markup. Preserve escaping and safe text APIs for untrusted values; do not bypass HTML-string semantics to satisfy display tests.
- Reuse a suitable server/shared browser. Confirm served artifacts match source and account for service-worker/cache staleness before diagnosing regressions. Do not erase user persistence just to obtain a clean test.
- For theme-aware UI controls, set an explicit theme-aware border color as well as foreground/background colors; native control borders may remain low-contrast when only `color-scheme` and page colors change. Keep Logo `settextcolor` styles at higher precedence than theme tokens.
- For DOM-driven numeric settings, clamp values using the current input element's `min`/`max` attributes rather than duplicating hardcoded limits in JS.
- Keep web settings in shared `Module` state, and route dialog events and Logo commands through one setter so UI, runtime value, and persistence stay synchronized. Use per-setting `localStorage` keys where reload persistence is intended, and guard storage access because it can be unavailable or throw.
- If a setting only has meaning in browser DOM context, make its setter an immediate no-op when `document` is unavailable and avoid repeated scattered DOM guards.
